practices.practice: Do not commit cluster connection strings or credentials to source control; read the Azure DocumentDB connection URI and credentials from environment variables and prefer storing secrets in Azure Key Vault, and do not log raw connection strings.

practices.practice: Instantiate one MongoClient per process and reuse it (singleton); initialize it once (outside request/handler scope) so serverless warm invocations reuse connections.
practices.prior_belief: Configure the MongoDB driver connection pool (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize) and timeouts (connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) appropriate for your concurrency; reuse a global client instance rather than creating a new client per request.

practices.practice: Set retryWrites=false in the connection string for Azure DocumentDB because the service does not support MongoDB retryable writes; do not rely on driver-level retryable-writes semantics without verifying service support.
practices.prior_belief: Use driver‑level options for retryable reads/writes where supported (retryReads/retryWrites) and be aware of differences in retry semantics between MongoDB drivers and Azure's MongoDB API; test retry behavior for your driver version.
practices.source_name: Migrate from Amazon DocumentDB to Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)

practices.practice: Always use TLS for all connections and prefer Private Endpoint / VNet integration (or firewall rules) to avoid exposing the cluster to the public internet; do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Use TLS/SSL for all connections to the cluster (enable ssl=true/ tls=true in connection string) and verify server certificates; prefer private endpoints or VNet integration to avoid exposing the cluster to public internet.

practices.practice: Create indexes to support common aggregation shapes: create a unique index on patient_id and a compound index {patient_id:1, visit_date:-1} to accelerate last-visit lookups and avoid blocking sorts by following the ESR (Equality → Sort → Range) rule.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes that support the aggregation pipeline: ensure fields used in $match and $sort (age/dob, diagnosis codes, last_visit_date, patient_id) are indexed with appropriate single or compound indexes (e.g., {patient_id:1, last_visit_date:-1}).

practices.practice: Index multikey/array fields that you filter on (e.g., diagnosis_codes) but be aware of multikey limitations and that multikey indexes cannot be fully covering for queries that need array semantics.
In aggregation pipelines push $match as early as possible and $project only required fields early so that index scans are used and intermediate memory/network work is reduced.
practices.prior_belief: Project only required fields in queries and aggregation ($project early) to reduce network and memory usage, and push $match as early as possible in pipelines so indexes can be used.

practices.practice: Run explain('executionStats') on queries and aggregation pipelines to verify index usage and plan shape, and for aggregations that produce large intermediates use allowDiskUse or persist results with $out/$merge.
practices.prior_belief: When performing heavy aggregations, use explain() and the MCP server tools to inspect the aggregation plan and confirm index usage; if an aggregation will produce large intermediate data, use allowDiskUse or write intermediate results to a collection ($out/$merge).

practices.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient faults (network blips, 429s) and design writes to be idempotent (use deterministic _id or idempotency keys) so retries are safe.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient errors (network timeouts, 429 / rate limit responses). Make writes idempotent when retries are used (e.g., upsert with a deterministic _id or idempotency key).

practices.practice: Tune driver connection-pool parameters by environment: small pools (maxPoolSize 3-5, minPoolSize 0) for serverless; larger pools and pre-warming for long-running OLTP servers, and always base values on expected concurrency.
Monitor RU consumption, latency, index usage and throughput with Azure Monitor and set autoscale or adequate provisioned throughput to avoid 429s during batch loads or heavy aggregations.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor RU consumption, latency, index usage and throughput with Azure Monitor and set autoscale or adequate provisioned throughput to avoid 429s during batch loads or heavy aggregations; test expected workloads against the cluster size (M30) before production use.

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and capture slow-query logs, index usage and failed requests (send to Log Analytics) and alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/connection saturation to inform index tuning and cost control.
practices.prior_belief: Audit and enable diagnostics/logging: capture slow query logs, Azure diagnostic settings, index usage and failed requests to inform index tuning and cost control.

practices.practice: For vector search, store embeddings as dense float arrays, normalize embeddings when using cosine similarity, and choose index type by scale: DiskANN for large production, HNSW for medium (≈50k), IVF for small/dev.
practices.prior_belief: For vector search, store embeddings as dense float arrays in a dedicated field and create the appropriate vector index (choose index type matching workload: HNSW for high‑recall, IVF/DiskANN for large scale); normalize vectors if using cosine similarity.

practices.practice: When seeding large datasets use bulk write techniques (insertMany / bulk executor), set ordered:false to improve throughput, tune batch sizes (client-side batches ~<=1000), and use throughput control or distributed ingestion to avoid 429s.
practices.prior_belief: For seeding large datasets, use bulk writes (bulk_write / insert_many with ordered=False) and tune batch sizes to avoid large single‑document/large‑transaction overhead; monitor RU consumption while seeding.

practices.practice: Avoid operations that return extremely large or unbounded result sets; use pagination (prefer range-based pagination over skip/limit), set cursor batchSize, and cap results to control memory and RU usage.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid operations that return extremely large documents or unbounded result sets; always use pagination (limit/skip or better yet range queries with a sort key) and set reasonable batchSize on cursors to control memory and RU usage.

practices.practice: When using $lookup ensure the join local and foreign fields are indexed and pre-filter inputs before the join to reduce the amount of data shuffled during the operation.
practices.prior_belief: Use server‑side aggregation ($group/$lookup/$facet) to reduce clientside joins when possible, but ensure supporting indexes exist for the $lookup local/foreign fields; prefer pipeline optimizations (pre-filtering) to reduce data shuffled in joins.

practices.practice: Protect backup artifacts and enable customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption at rest when handling regulated healthcare data and verify restore/test procedures and retention policies.

practices.practice: Tune indexes for cardinality: avoid indexing low‑cardinality boolean flags unless they are highly selective, and consider partial or sparse indexes to reduce index size for fields with many missing values.
practices.prior_belief: Tune indexes for cardinality: avoid indexing low‑cardinality boolean flags unless used heavily in selective queries; consider partial or sparse indexes if supported to reduce index size for fields like diagnosis codes where only a subset of docs have values.

practices.practice: Run seeding and schema-changing operations first against a staging/test database on the same cluster tier to observe RU usage, index-build time and query plans before applying to production.

practices.practice: For expensive or frequently-run analytical aggregations precompute care‑gap flags as materialized results or periodic batch jobs writing to a prioritized outreach collection instead of computing them ad‑hoc for every user request.

practices.practice: Apply the principle of least privilege: avoid using the cluster admin key for app operations and prefer Microsoft Entra ID / managed identities or per-app users with the minimal required roles (e.g., readWrite on the app database).

practices.practice: For local development, run the DocumentDB gateway Docker image and connect with TLS on port 10260; use env-driven configuration and seeded sample data for dev/prod parity.
Prefer the native textSearch / $search capabilities and built-in search indexes over the community $text index for full-text search on Azure DocumentDB.
